L461: Scientific achievements of Robert Schatten.
L462: Schatten
L463: dealt with Banach spaces and linear transformations in Hilbert spaces,
L464: among other things. Schatten’s main mathematical achievement was
L465: initiating the study of tensor products of Banach spaces. The concepts
L466: of “cross norms”, associated norms, largest, smallest, and uniform “cross
L467: norms”, which are mostly derived from him, or at least were first care-
L468: fully studied in his articles. His name has been immortalized in Schatten
L469: classes (see [7], [27], [29]).
L470: He wrote 13 mathematical papers and two books [S9], [S12]. The
L471: first book on normed tensor products was the 1950 monograph [S9],
L472: which summarized the state of the art at the time. The second book
L473: from 1960 [S12] is about operator ideals on Hilbert spaces.
L474: 2.1. Tensor products of Banach spaces. Tensor products first
L475: appeared in Functional Analysis in the late 1930s in Murray and John
L476: von Neumann’s [26] paper on rings of operators on Hilbert spaces. The
L477: first systematic studies of tensor products in Banach spaces were initi-
L478: ated in the forties: Schatten (1943, 1946 in [S2], [S3], [S4]), Dunford–
L479: Schatten (1946 in [S5]), and Schatten–von Neumann (1946, 1948 in [S6],
L480: [S8]).
L481: Schatten’s main achievement in this field was the initiation of re-
L482: search on tensor products of Banach spaces. The concepts of crossnorm,
L483: associated crossnorm, greatest crossnorm, reflexive crossnorm, uniform
L484: crossnorm are mostly derived from him, or at least were first thoroughly
L485: explored in his papers.
L486: The first book on normed tensor products was R. Schatten’s 1950
L487: monograph [S9], which summarized the state-of-the-art at the time (the

L560: 2.3. Other papers by Schatten
L561: We will discuss results from Schatten’s papers that have not been
L562: previously cited.
L563: In a paper [S7], published in 1947, Schatten showed that if X0 is
L564: a closed subspace of a Banach space X, and there is a projection of
L565: X onto X0 with bound 1, then the greatest crossnorm γ on the tensor
L566: product X ⊗Y is an extension of the greatest crossnorm on X0 ⊗Y for
L567: any Banach space Y (see [S7, Lemma 2, p. 323]; see also [S9, Lemma
L568: 3.7, p. 55]).
L569: In a paper [S10], published in 1950, Schatten discussed two methods
L570: for completing a linear sequence space c00 of real sequences (u1, u2, . . .)
L571: having only a finite number of non-zero terms, with respect to a stan-
L572: dard “symmetric’” and normalized norm ϕ(u1, u2, . . .). The first method
L573: (strong closure) consists in the construction of all sequences (u1, u2, . . .)
L574: for which limn→∞ϕ(u1, . . . , un, 0, 0, . . .) < ∞; the second method is the
L575: Cantor–M´eray completion of a metric space7. The Cantor–M´eray com-
L576: pletion is always included in the strong closure and examples are given
L577: in Schatten’s paper which show that the two can be distinct.
L578: In a paper [S11], published in 1957, Schatten proved the interesting
L579: result that the unit ball in the space K(H) of compact operators on a
L580: separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space H has no extreme points,
L581: and hence by the Krein–Milman theorem is not isomorphic to any con-
L582: jugate space X∗of a Banach space X. Important tools in the proof was
L583: the so-called “polar representation” of a compact operator on H and
L584: methods of topological tensor products.
L585: Schatten’s 1962 paper [S13] initially resembles the approximation
L586: theorems of Weierstrass and M¨untz, but the main part of this expository
L587: paper was a discussion on the non-aproximation theorem.
